title: Quickstart Pathfinder — interaction explainer canvas and screenshot choreography
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create an interaction-focused visual canvas for the Quickstart landing page that explains first-run user pathways with sequential screenshot choreography, micro-interaction prototypes, and an assets package for engineering and docs. This ticket ships a living spec: high-fidelity artboards, a short explainer animation, annotated screenshot variants for different product states (empty, example data, error), and a developer-ready sprite/export guide.
scope: Deliver a deterministic set of hero and step visuals that can be reused across marketing, docs, and product; include light/dark color variants, optimized PNG/JPEG exports, and a single page Figma file with components and tokens. Not in scope: full localized copy translations or backend feature work.
deliverables: Three hero compositions: static, animated-CTA, and compact mobile
Sequential screenshot set (5 states) with overlay callouts
Annotation page with dev export rules and screenshot choreography
acceptance_criteria: Design review approved by PM and Engineering design lead
All hero variants exported and uploaded to Drive with naming conventions
Prototype demonstrates the exact micro-interaction timing for the animated CTA
Screenshot set includes accessible contrast checks and alt-text drafts
Assets follow the export guide and build team can reproduce hero in the product repo using provided sprites
tasks: Audit existing quickstart screenshots and find gaps — Ava
Design three hero compositions and iterate — Diego
Produce sequential screenshots for empty/example/error states — Noor Patel
Create 6s explainer animation and export MP4/GIF — Diego

Write annotation/spec page for engineers with screenshot choreography — Diego
Schedule design review and record feedback — Ava
accessibility_notes: All text layers must meet AA contrast at both 14px and 18px sizes. Provide high-contrast screenshot variants for low-vision viewers. Include concise alt text drafts for each exported image in the annotation page. Motion in the explainer animation must have a reduced-motion variant—supply a static sequence and a short fade-only animation.
